title: Noisy Supervision for Correcting Misaligned Cadaster Maps Without Perfect Ground Truth Data
mechanism: A multi-resolution network predicts a dense displacement field that moves misaligned map polygons onto image evidence, trained on the noisy data itself and applied iteratively so dataset alignment improves round by round.
adaptation: Train a small U-Net (image + jittered label in, 2-channel displacement out) on synthetic jitter drawn from our measured offset distribution (48% within 1 px, 64% within 2 px) applied to high-confidence snapped labels (ARTS, strong ridges); apply to all train crack labels, two rounds; then train the house model.
min_experiment: Only if the ridge-snap arm passes. Arm: learned-alignment labels; baseline: ridge-snap arm and house. Kill if n.d. vs ridge-snap.
evidence: R: cadaster/OSM building alignment on aerial imagery (web search listing only; numbers not read).
